title: Wildcard Matching
spaceBreakdown:
- int variables i, j, starIdx, match, n, m: 6 scalars → O(1)
- no containers, no recursion, no heap allocation
- not counted: input strings s, p
approach: Use two pointers (`i` for `s`, `j` for `p`) scanning left to right. When a `*` is encountered, record its position and the current `i`; the star initially matches zero characters. On any later mismatch, backtrack: reset `j` to just after the star and advance `i` by one (the star now consumes one more character). After consuming all of `s`, skip any trailing `*` in `p` and check that the pattern is exhausted. This greedy backtracking is correct because each `*` only needs to be expanded lazily - if a match exists, trying the shortest expansion first and growing on failure will find it.
hints: When the pattern contains a `*`, it can swallow any number of characters. If you are scanning left to right and hit a mismatch *after* a `*`, what two positions would you need to remember so you can retry with the `*` consuming one more character?

Two pointers with backtracking. Pointer `i` tracks `s`, `j` tracks `p`. On seeing `*`, save `starIdx = j` and `match = i`, then advance `j`. On mismatch with a saved star, set `j = starIdx + 1` and `i = ++match`. Example: `s = "aa"`, `p = "*"` - star saved at j=0, match=0; the loop backtracks twice until `i` reaches 2, then the trailing-star check passes.

**Empty string with star** - pattern is a single `*`, string is empty.
`Input: s = "", p = "*"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: skipping the trailing-star loop after the main while → returns `false`

**Star must match zero characters** - the `*` sits between two literal segments that are already adjacent in `s`.
`Input: s = "abc", p = "a*bc"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: forcing every `*` to consume at least one character (incrementing `i` when recording the star) → returns `false`

**Star at end, string longer** - `*` is the last pattern char but `s` has remaining characters.
`Input: s = "abc", p = "a*"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: returning `j == m` immediately when the main loop ends without skipping trailing `*` → returns `false`

**No valid match after star** - star expands but the tail of `p` never aligns.
`Input: s = "ab", p = "*c"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: returning `true` whenever any `*` was seen, without exhausting the pattern → returns `true`

**Multiple consecutive stars** - pattern has `***`, which is equivalent to a single `*`.
`Input: s = "ab", p = "***"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: treating each `*` as requiring a separate non-empty segment → returns `false`

followUps.q: What if `*` must match at least one character (like `+` in regex)?
followUps.a: When recording a star, set `match = i + 1` instead of `match = i` so the first backtrack already forces the star to consume one character. The rest of the algorithm stays the same. TC remains O(nm), SC O(1).

followUps.q: What if the pattern can also contain character classes like `[a-z]`?
followUps.a: Replace the single-character comparison `p[j] == s[i] || p[j] == '?'` with a helper that checks whether `s[i]` falls in the class described at `p[j]`. You would need to parse the class boundaries first. TC becomes O(nm) with an added class-parsing cost, SC O(1) if classes are matched inline.

followUps.q: What if `s` is a stream too large to fit in memory?
followUps.a: Process `s` character by character without storing it. The two-pointer algorithm only looks at the current character of `s`, so it works in a single pass. You still need the full pattern `p` in memory. TC O(nm) worst case, SC O(m) for the pattern.
